What is the minimum number of years of education all children must have in Denmark?
At least ten years (there is compulsory education, not compulsory school attendance).
What does it cost to go to the folkeskole?
It is free for all children.
How long does the folkeskole last?
10 years: the reception class (børnehaveklasse) + years 1–9.
About how old are children when they start in the reception class (børnehaveklasse)?
About six years old.
What do children begin to learn in the reception class?
Letters and numbers.
What are the folkeskole's three stages?
Early years (reception class–year 3), middle years (years 4–6) and upper years (years 7–9).
Is year 10 voluntary or compulsory?
Voluntary. About half of the pupils sign up.
Besides at your own school, where can you take year 10?
At an efterskole (boarding school) or a free vocational school (fri fagskole).
Which law sets the framework for the folkeskole?
The Folkeskole Act (Folkeskoleloven).
What must children at free schools and private schools learn compared with the folkeskole?
The same as in the folkeskole (the teaching must match the folkeskole's standard).
Do parents have to pay for free schools and private schools?
Yes, parents pay the school directly. In the folkeskole they do not pay.
What four purposes does the folkeskole have (prepare, familiar, understanding, ...)?
Prepare pupils for further education, make them familiar with Danish culture and history, give them an understanding of other countries and cultures, and show how people and nature affect each other.
Who has the right to form a pupils' council (elevråd)?
Pupils at schools with year 5 or higher.
Who makes up a pupils' council?
At least one pupil from each class.
What is the minimum number of pupil representatives on the school board?
At least two.
Who has the majority on the school board?
The parents.
Who makes up the school board?
Representatives of parents, staff and pupils – possibly up to two from local business, youth education or associations.
From which year do pupils get grades in the folkeskole?
From year 8 (at least twice a year).
What is the Danish grading scale called, and what are the highest and lowest grades?
The 7-point scale. The highest is 12, the lowest is -3.
What is a meddelelsesbog (report book)?
The teacher's assessment of how the pupil is doing academically (and possibly socially) – from the reception class up to and including year 9.
How often, at minimum, are parents invited to a school–home meeting, and how long does it last?
At least once a year; it usually lasts about 15 minutes.
How often are class parents' meetings held?
At most schools one to two times a year.
What can a class council (klasseråd) do, among other things?
Arrange class parties and school camps, deal with social problems (e.g. teasing) and pass criticism on to the school board.
When must a pupil be offered special education?
When the pupil needs support in at least nine lessons a week.
What is an efterskole?
A school where pupils live and are taught – for years 8, 9 or 10. It costs money.
Do the independent primary schools (frie grundskoler) receive public support?
Most receive financial support from the state.
Is education in Denmark usually free or paid?
Usually free.
What does it mean that Denmark is called a knowledge society?
That more and more people have jobs where knowledge is the most important resource.
What is FGU?
Preparatory basic education – for young people under 25 without a youth education or a job who need preparatory help.
What is STU?
Specially designed youth education – for young people under 25 with special needs. It does not in itself give access to other education.
What four upper secondary programmes are there?
stx (general upper secondary exam), hhx (business), htx (technical) and hf.
How long do stx, hhx and htx take – and how long does hf take?
stx, hhx and htx take three years. hf takes two years.
What is hhx about, and which exam do you get?
Business: economics, marketing, international economics. You get the business upper secondary exam (at a business gymnasium).
What is htx about, and which exam do you get?
Science and technology subjects. You get the technical upper secondary exam (at a technical gymnasium).
Which programmes is the hf exam especially aimed at?
Short and medium-length higher education at university colleges and academies of professional higher education.
What do all four upper secondary programmes give access to?
Higher education.
How many different vocational education programmes are there?
More than 100.
How is a vocational education programme structured?
A basic course at a vocational school and a main course where school is combined with practical training (usually in a company).
How long can a vocational education take?
Between 1½ and 5½ years.
What do you get if you cannot find an apprenticeship after the basic course?
Training at a school training centre – and a school training allowance instead of wages.
What do eud, euv and eux stand for?
eud = for young people; euv = for adults over 25; eux = vocational education combined with an upper secondary exam (journeyman's certificate + vocational upper secondary exam).
What four main areas do the vocational programmes cover?
Office, trade and business services; Food, agriculture and hospitality; Technology, construction and transport; Health, care and education.
How many academies of professional higher education are there, and how long does such a programme take?
Seven academies. The programme typically takes about two years (with an internship).
How many university colleges (professionshøjskoler) are there, and how long does a professional bachelor's degree take?
Seven university colleges. The programme normally takes three to four years (with an internship).
Give examples of professional bachelor's programmes.
Primary school teacher, midwife, nurse, social worker, pedagogue (early-childhood educator), physiotherapist, diploma engineer, journalist.
